# Phase 3 results: MPSoC composition benchmark and interpreter v3

*Generated by `phase3/runner/analyze_phase3.py` from the 990 `metrics.json` files in `phase3/results/phase3_run/` (source of truth) and `compose_results.jsonl`. Do not hand-edit: change the template `phase3/runner/templates/PHASE3_RESULTS.md.tmpl` or the script and rerun. Every number below, including the numbers in the prose, is filled in by the script.*

## Design in one paragraph

6 models (llama3.2:3b, gemma3:4b, deepseek-coder:6.7b, qwen2.5-coder:7b, llama3.1:latest, qwen2.5-coder:14b) x 11 repair tasks (8 real MPSoC leaf modules + 3 seeded RISC-V/NoC modules) x 5 conditions x N=3 replicates = 990 runs, temperature 0.1, one shared budget of 6 LLM calls per run for every condition. Protocol `feedback_first_v2`: the defective input is evaluated first and the condition's feedback on it goes into the first LLM call. Every candidate is always scored with simulation + lint + synthesis; conditions differ only in what is fed back.

| condition | what the model sees |
|---|---|
| baseline | simulation feedback only; stops at the first simulation pass, **including on the unmodified input (0 LLM calls)** |
| raw_adv | simulation + filtered raw Verilator/Yosys warning and error lines; stops at clean_pass |
| sem_adv_v2 | simulation + production interpreter directives + the same raw lines |
| sem_adv_v3 | simulation + v3 interpreter directives + the same raw lines |
| sem_esc_restart_v3 | starts like baseline but behind a clean-pass gate (a generic "fails synthesis sign-off" message, no tool detail); escalates to v3 after 2 identical failure signatures; one blank-slate restart |

Metrics: `func_pass` (Icarus compiles, testbench prints ALL TESTS PASSED); `clean_pass` = func_pass AND structurally clean (Yosys succeeds, 0 latches, 0 logic loops, 0 Verilator MULTIDRIVEN/UNOPTFLAT/LATCH/WIDTHTRUNC); `silent structural pass` = func_pass but not clean. Sim-silent tasks (6): the defective input already passes simulation (MuxPC, execute_mux, mem_wb_mux, mux3, register_1bit, riscv_alu_flags). Sim-visible tasks (5): the input fails simulation (Address_select, ni_flit_pack, noc_xbar4, register_32bit, register_4bit).

**How to read the statistics.** Every rate is k/N with a Wilson 95% interval. Paired contrasts match runs on (model, task, rep), but the runs are independent draws (no shared seed), so the matching is a stratification, not a replay. Two views are given: an exact McNemar p on the discordant pairs (run level; valid for these specific (model, task) cells), and a bootstrap CI plus sign-flip p over the 66 (model, task) cells (cell level; respects that the 3 replicates of a cell are correlated). Table T12 shows the correlation is real: the cell-level CI is about 1.7 times wider than the Wilson CI, and most cells are unanimous. **Where the two views disagree, the cell-level view is the one to quote for a general claim.** An interpreter win counts only if clean_pass AND semantic_fired hold in the same run. Under the feedback-first protocol the interpreter fires on the defective input, so sf is 198/198 for v3 and does not discriminate; the discriminating comparison is v3 against raw_adv, which shows the same raw text and has the same budget.

## Key findings

1. **A simulation-only loop signs off structurally defective RTL; running the structural tools removes most of that (T1, T2, T2b, T11).** Baseline makes 0 LLM calls in 108 of its 108 sim-silent runs (it stops at the input) and ends with a silent structural pass in 108/108 (100%, 97–100); over all tasks 122/198 (62%, 55–68) of baseline runs pass simulation but are structurally dirty. With tools that falls to 11 (raw_adv), 5 (v2) and 1 (v3) of 198. Sim-silent clean_pass: raw 70/108 (65%, 55–73), v2 86/108 (80%, 71–86), v3 88/108 (81%, 73–88), escalation 91/108 (84%, 76–90). On latch-bearing tasks, runs ending latch-free rise from 35/144 (24%, 18–32) (baseline) to 127/144 (88%, 82–92) (v3); latch events on the final RTL fall from 180 on the inputs to 138 (baseline) and 3 (v3). *Scope:* baseline's 0 on sim-silent tasks is fixed by the protocol (an AutoChip loop stops at the first simulation pass), so this measures the value of running the structural checks at all, not a model-quality gap.

2. **Interpreting the tool output beats showing it raw, at lower cost (T3, T3b, T3c, T5, T10).** sem_adv_v3 146/198 (74%, 67–79) vs raw_adv 117/198 (59%, 52–66): +14.6 points, cell-level CI [+3.5, +26.3], sign-flip p 0.016, v3-only/raw-only pairs 43/14. With the same raw text and the same budget, v3 changes LLM calls per run by -23.3% and tokens per run by -23.2% (calls -0.76 [-1.33, -0.20], tokens -1019 [-1671, -354], cell-level CIs exclude 0) and costs 4580.0 tokens per clean pass against 7440.1 for raw. It also gets there faster: clean after the first LLM call in 122/198 (62%, 55–68) of runs vs 92/198 (46%, 40–53) (raw) and 33/198 (17%, 12–22) (baseline). Production v2 also beats raw on sim-silent tasks (+14.8 points, cell-level CI [+0.0, +29.6]) and is neutral on sim-visible ones (+2.2). *Not uniform:* after Holm correction only qwen2.5-coder:7b is individually significant (+27.3 points, Holm p 0.023); llama3.1 is +3.0 and the 14B model is +0.0 (ceiling); per task v3 is below raw on mem_wb_mux (-11.1) and ni_flit_pack (-16.7) and level on noc_xbar4 (+0.0).

3. **The v3 upgrade fixes coverage; a gain in pass rate over v2 is not established at this N (T4, T4b).** v2 produced no directive on the defective input of register_1bit (0/18 runs) and ni_flit_pack (0/18); v3 fires on both in 18/18 and 18/18 with the intended class (ASYNC_RESET, WIDTHTRUNC). On register_4bit and register_32bit v2 directed LATCH+UNUSEDSIGNAL (the misleading class); v3 directs MISSING_CLOCK. On the four focus tasks clean_pass is 42/72 (58%, 47–69) (v2) vs 50/72 (69%, 58–79) (v3): +11.1 points, cell-level CI [-9.7, +31.9], p 0.391 (McNemar 0.152): favourable direction, interval includes 0. Pooled over all tasks v3 vs v2 is +5.6 ([-2.5, +14.1]). Per task: register_1bit 12 -> 15 of 18 (v2's clean passes there were 9 without any v2 directive; sf-gated wins v2 3/18 (17%, 6–39) vs v3 15/18 (83%, 61–94)); register_32bit 12 -> 15, register_4bit 11 -> 14 (v3 returns to the baseline level of 15 and 14, it does not exceed it); **ni_flit_pack: v3 fires correctly but clean_pass is 7 -> 6 of 18 (no gain).** *In-sample:* v3 was written from the real logs of these same tasks.

4. **Gains are largest for the 3B to 7B models; the 14B model is at ceiling with any tool feedback, llama3.1 (8B) gains little, and raw tool text can hurt a small model on defects that simulation already reveals (T6, T6b).** sem_adv_v3 minus raw_adv is +24.2 (3B), +18.2 (4B), +15.2 (6.7B), +27.3 (7B), +3.0 (8B), +0.0 (14B) points, of which only the 7B model survives Holm correction. qwen2.5-coder:14b is 18/18 (100%, 82–100) on sim-silent tasks under every tool condition. qwen2.5-coder:7b reaches 15/15 (100%, 80–100) (sim-visible) and 18/18 (100%, 82–100) (sim-silent) with v3. The smallest models remain lowest overall (v3: llama3.2:3b 11/18 (61%, 39–80) silent, 2/15 (13%, 4–38) visible). **Harm:** on sim-visible tasks llama3.2:3b scores 9/15 (60%, 36–80) with simulation feedback alone but 1/15 (7%, 1–30) with raw tool text (-53.3 points, McNemar p 0.008, uncorrected across 6 models); escalation restores it to 8/15 (53%, 30–75). The six models differ in family as well as size, so size alone cannot be credited.

5. **Escalation has the highest clean_pass and the fewest tool rounds of the tool conditions, but its gain over always-on v3 is not established, and how much of it comes from the generic gate message cannot be separated (T3, T5, T5b, T10).** sem_esc_restart_v3 158/198 (80%, 74–85) vs sem_adv_v3 146/198 (74%, 67–79): +6.1 points (McNemar p 0.043, cell-level p 0.180, cell-level CI [-1.5, +14.1]). Tool-feedback rounds per run change by -47.5% (-1.19 [-1.72, -0.67], CI excludes 0), but LLM calls (+0.48 [-0.07, +1.03]) and tokens (+420 [-291, +1127]) per run are not lower (point estimates up, CIs include 0). Against raw_adv the gain is large and robust (+20.7, cell-level CI [+11.1, +30.8]). 109 runs never escalated and 105/109 (96%, 91–99) were clean using only the generic sign-off message; the 89/198 (45%, 38–52) runs that did escalate ended 53/89 (60%, 49–69) clean at 5.0 calls per run. Of its 158 clean passes only 48 are interpreter wins (sf and clean); 110 had no interpreter output. Escalation is strongest on sim-visible tasks (67/90 (74%, 65–82) vs v3 58/90 (64%, 54–74)).

6. **Composition into the real designs: tools decide whether the designs synthesize at all, and leaf-level clean_pass was sufficient for composition in every case (T7, T7bounds, T7c).** The unrepaired references fail top-level synthesis (register_1bit's async-reset crash) with baseline at 0/18 (0%, 0–18) in mesh2x2, mesh3x3 and mpsoc, since baseline never touches that sim-silent leaf. Top-level synthesis pass (mesh2x2 = mesh3x3 counts, same three leaves): raw 15/18 (83%, 61–94), v2 13/18 (72%, 49–88), v3 16/18 (89%, 67–97), escalation 18/18 (100%, 82–100); mpsoc: raw 13/18 (72%, 49–88), v2 12/18 (67%, 44–84), v3 16/18 (89%, 67–97), escalation 15/18 (83%, 61–94). Reaching the golden bound (pass and no more latch cells than the all-golden repair): mesh raw 10/18 (56%, 34–75), v3 15/18 (83%, 61–94), escalation 16/18 (89%, 67–97); mpsoc raw 8/18 (44%, 25–66), v3 14/18 (78%, 55–91), escalation 13/18 (72%, 49–88). Whenever every composed leaf was clean_pass, the composed design reached the bound: 32/32 (mesh2x2), 32/32 (mesh3x3), 27/27 (mpsoc); no composition-only failure occurred. *Scope:* synthesis only, not simulation of the composed system; N=18 groups per cell, so the differences between v2, v3 and escalation are not statistically resolved (paired v3 vs raw at bound, mesh: 6/1, McNemar p 0.125).

7. **What is left over is model capability and a functional-regression risk, not unfixed structure (T8, T8b, T9).** For sem_adv_v3, 52 runs did not end clean and 1 of them still had a structural defect; the other 51 failed to compile or to simulate (T9). Over all runs 124 final candidates failed to compile, 66 from gemma3:4b and 42 from llama3.2:3b, 0 from the 14B model; 124/124 of them were well-formed fenced code blocks, so these are model syntax and declaration errors, not extraction failures. **Regressions:** no run was clean at some iteration and worse at the end (0; runs stop at the first clean candidate). But 92 runs lost a simulation pass they had at some iteration, all with tool feedback: raw 36, v2 22, v3 23, escalation 11. Among runs whose input passed simulation, the final RTL fails simulation in 32/108 (30%, 22–39) (raw), 20/108 (19%, 12–27) (v3) and 11/108 (10%, 6–17) (escalation). A keep-best-so-far rule would have restored func_pass (v3 170/198 (86%, 80–90), escalation 179/198 (90%, 85–94); a post hoc calculation on the logged trajectories, not a measured condition).

8. **Null and negative results (T2, T2c, T3, T3c).** On the sim-visible tasks, where baseline actually runs, raw tool text adds nothing over simulation feedback (raw 47/90 (52%, 42–62) vs baseline 46/90 (51%, 41–61), +1.1 points) and v3 is +13.3 points (cell-level CI [-5.6, +32.2], includes 0). noc_xbar4 (MULTIDRIVEN) is at baseline level under every condition (baseline 10, raw 9, v2 10, v3 9 of 18 although the interpreter fires on all 18 inputs); riscv_alu_flags stays at 9/18 under v3; mem_wb_mux and ni_flit_pack are below raw under v3 (T3c). The benefit is therefore concentrated in sim-silent defects and mid-size models; it is not universal.

## STITCH vs baseline: where it was better, where it was not

Read this before quoting any pooled baseline comparison. The pooled gap (T1) mixes two different things: on the 6 sim-silent tasks baseline never calls the model (it stops at the input), so its 0% there is set by the protocol; the like-for-like comparison is the 5 sim-visible tasks, where baseline runs the model like every other condition.

| where | comparison | STITCH | baseline | difference | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sim-silent tasks (0 LLM calls for baseline) | raw / v2 / v3 / escalation clean_pass vs baseline | 70/108 (65%, 55–73) / 86/108 (80%, 71–86) / 88/108 (81%, 73–88) / 91/108 (84%, 76–90) | 0/108 (0%, 0–3) | set by protocol | every tool condition beats it; this is the "simulation signs off defective RTL" finding, not a repair-quality gap |
| sim-visible tasks | raw_adv | 47/90 (52%, 42–62) | 46/90 (51%, 41–61) | +1.1 points, cell CI [-16.7, +17.8] | no difference |
| sim-visible tasks | sem_adv_v3 | 58/90 (64%, 54–74) | 46/90 (51%, 41–61) | +13.3 points, cell CI [-5.6, +32.2], cell p 0.205 | favourable direction, not established |
| sim-visible tasks | sem_esc_restart_v3 | 67/90 (74%, 65–82) | 46/90 (51%, 41–61) | +23.3 points, cell CI [+8.9, +37.8], cell p 0.005 | **better than baseline** |
| sim-visible, deepseek-coder:6.7b | escalation | 15/15 (100%, 80–100) | 9/15 (60%, 36–80) | +40.0, McNemar p 0.031 | better (uncorrected across 6 models) |
| sim-visible, qwen2.5-coder:7b | escalation | 15/15 (100%, 80–100) | 9/15 (60%, 36–80) | +40.0, McNemar p 0.031 | better (uncorrected across 6 models) |
| all tasks, simulation correctness | func_pass raw / v2 / v3 / escalation | 128/198 (65%, 58–71) / 140/198 (71%, 64–77) / 147/198 (74%, 68–80) / 168/198 (85%, 79–89) | 168/198 (85%, 79–89) | always-on tool feedback is **lower**; escalation equal | **baseline better or equal**: tool feedback makes models break designs that already passed simulation (T8) |
| sim-visible, llama3.2:3b | raw / v2 / v3 / escalation | 1/15 (7%, 1–30) / 4/15 (27%, 11–52) / 2/15 (13%, 4–38) / 8/15 (53%, 30–75) | 9/15 (60%, 36–80) | always-on tool feedback is **lower** (raw: -53.3 points, p 0.008); escalation near baseline | **baseline better** for this model |
| register_4bit / register_32bit (sim-visible) | raw / v2 / v3 (of 18 each) | 10 / 11 / 14 and 11 / 12 / 15 | 14 and 15 | raw and v2 below baseline; v3 back to baseline | baseline better than raw and v2; v3 equal |

**How much of the sim-silent gain is the interpreter?** Escalation's gate message alone ("fails synthesis sign-off", no detail) accompanies 66/108 (61%, 52–70) clean sim-silent runs with no interpreter output at all, out of 91/108 (84%, 76–90) clean; only 25/108 (23%, 16–32) are interpreter wins. A baseline that is merely told sign-off failed would therefore probably capture much of the sim-silent gain without any interpretation. This control arm was not run, so the split between "being told" and "being told what" is not measured; what the interpreter adds beyond raw text is measured (finding 2).

**Summary.** STITCH was clearly better than baseline (i) at surfacing defects that simulation cannot see, (ii) on sim-visible defects when escalation is used, and (iii) than raw tool text. It was not better than baseline on simulation correctness when always on, for the smallest model on defects simulation already reveals, or for raw/v2 on the two register tasks.

## Limitations

1. **Precision is lower than the run count suggests.** 990 runs are 330 (model, task, condition) cells of 3 correlated replicates at temperature 0.1; most cells are unanimous (T12). Wilson intervals treat runs as independent and are therefore optimistic; the cell-level intervals are about 1.7 times wider. Per-model and per-task comparisons have 33 or 18 pairs and low power, so "no detectable difference" is not evidence of no effect.
2. **Baseline is protocol-defined at 0 on sim-silent tasks.** AutoChip stops at the first simulation pass, which on these tasks is the unmodified input. Tools-versus-none on sim-silent tasks therefore measures whether structural checks are run, not model ability; the like-for-like contrast is the sim-visible stratum (T2, T3), where raw text was neutral.
3. **The escalation condition includes a one-bit sign-off signal.** Its gate message ("fails synthesis sign-off", no detail) is more information than baseline receives, and 110 of its 158 clean passes came with no interpreter output. Phase 3 cannot separate the gate message from the interpreter for this condition; a control arm (baseline plus the same message) would (not run).
4. **The v2-to-v3 result is in-sample.** v3 rules were written from the real logs of these tasks (`PROD_V2_ON_REAL_LOGS.md`), so improved coverage on register_1bit, register_4bit, register_32bit and ni_flit_pack is evidence that the rules work on the defects they were built for, not that they generalise. The pass-rate difference to v2 is not statistically established (finding 3).
5. **The clean_pass metric and the interpreter share a vocabulary.** clean_pass penalises the same warning classes the interpreter directs (latch, loop, MULTIDRIVEN, WIDTHTRUNC, Yosys errors). Correctness beyond the task testbench is not established.
6. **Phase 3 feedback is not byte-identical to Sets 1 and 3.** Raw feedback is the same filtered text for every Phase 3 condition, and Phase 3 raw text is far longer than what the production sem_adv showed in Sets 1 and 3 (98 vs 2 and 5,239 vs 40 lines in the earlier audit recorded in `CC_INTEGRATION_REPORT.md`). Phase 3 sem_adv_v2 is therefore not directly comparable to earlier sem_adv numbers, and results are not pooled across phases.
7. **Six models, several families.** Size, family and coder specialisation vary together (T6), so no size effect is isolated. Two families appear twice (qwen2.5-coder 7B and 14B; llama 3.2 3B and llama 3.1 8B), and there is no frontier model.
8. **Task set and benchmark.** 11 tasks (8 real leaves, 3 seeded), one code base, three composed designs. mesh2x2 and mesh3x3 share the same three leaves, so their identical results are one observation, not two.
9. **Composition is synthesis-only.** The composed designs are checked with Yosys, not simulated; the leaves are spliced by module name into a compile-only sanitised copy (`phase3/designs/SANITISATION.md`). A leaf that failed to compile leaves the reference module in place.
10. **Iteration budget and stopping.** All conditions share 6 LLM calls, which removes the Pass@6/Pass@8 confound of Set 3, but every non-baseline run stops at the first clean candidate, so regressions from a clean state cannot occur by construction; runs that end below their best earlier candidate (T8) are functional losses.
11. **Toolchain.** The manifests of all six models report Yosys 0.69+71, Verilator 5.053; manifests record the last invocation only, so a mid-run toolchain change would not show. The gates and tests were developed on older local tools (Yosys 0.33, Verilator 5.020, Icarus 12.0).
12. **Multiple comparisons.** T3, T3b, T3c and T6b contain many contrasts. Holm correction is applied within the per-model and per-task families only; the pooled and per-stratum contrasts (v3 vs raw, v3 vs v2, escalation vs v3, tools vs none) are the ones named in advance in `PHASE3_EXPLAINED.md` section 7, and everything finer is exploratory.
13. **Run hygiene.** 3 transient Ollama timeouts (llama3.2:3b) were each superseded by a later successful re-run of the same cell (3 of 3 confirmed from master_log order); `master_log.json` holds 993 entries for 990 runs and is not used for results.

## Reproduce

```
python phase3/runner/analyze_phase3.py
```

Seeded (seed 20260925; bootstrap 10,000 resamples, sign-flip 20,000). Written next to this file: `phase3_analysis.json` (every number, machine-readable), `phase3_tables.md`, `phase3_regressions.csv`, `figures/fig_p3_*.png` (the paper figures).
